about.title: Avalon Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Avalon runs differently than most California towns — golf carts serve as everyday transportation along Wrigley Terrace Road, Wrigley Road, Marilla Avenue, and Saint Catherine Way, and nearly every good that reaches this Catalina Island community arrives by boat. That reliance on golf carts, marine equipment, and imported consumer goods means a defective battery, faulty brake system, cracked hull fitting, or mislabeled product can cause real harm fast. Los Angeles County crash records show 11 injury collisions and 17 people hurt here in the most recent year tracked, with Saturday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. showing the heaviest activity — a window when golf cart and pedestrian traffic both climb. California product liability law generally lets an injured person hold a manufacturer, distributor, or retailer accountable for a defective product without having to prove negligence. If a product failed and hurt you or someone you love in Avalon, LawProactive can connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who handles these cases.

whyChoose.title: Why Avalon Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: California generally applies strict liability to defective products, meaning you may not need to prove the manufacturer was careless — just that the product was defective and caused your injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and even the local retailer who sold a defective golf cart part or marine product can potentially be held accountable under California law.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters Early On
items.desc: Because product defect claims often hinge on physical evidence, an attorney can advise you right away on keeping the item safe for inspection, which can be especially important with limited shipping options on the island.

items.question: I was hurt in a golf cart accident on Avalon's streets — is that a product liability case?
items.answer: It depends on why the golf cart failed. If a brake, steering component, or battery malfunctioned due to a design or manufacturing defect, that could support a product liability claim against the maker or distributor rather than just a standard traffic claim. An independent attorney can review the details and figure out which type of claim fits your situation.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California generally allows strict liability claims for defective products, so the focus is usually on whether the product itself was unreasonably dangerous and caused your injury, not on proving carelessness by the maker.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it in the same condition and location if possible, and avoid repairs or disposal. On an island like Avalon where replacement parts often have to be shipped in, it can be tempting to fix or discard a broken item quickly — but preserving it can be important evidence for a claim.
